2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule as stated in the writ petition, are that when the Noakhali District Head Quarter was under threat of soil erosion, the then Government acquired 608.23 acres of land from various plots of various Khatians of Mouza 170 Mirwarishpur, 171 Nazirpur, 237 Alipur, 238 Chowmuhani, 239 Ganipur, and 241 Narottampur, Police Station-Begumgonj through Land Acquisition Case No. 3(1) of 1941-42 for shifting the District Head Quarter Noakhali therein. Subsequently, the then Government took a decision to shift the District Headquarter Noakhali to Maijdee. Accordingly, the original owners of the land were not evicted from the acquired land. Meanwhile, during State Acquisition operation the acquired land was recorded in the name of the Government in Khas Khatian No. 1. However, the Government took a decision to lease out the acquired land to the different persons who are in possession including the petitioners and accordingly the Government took salami from them. The petitioners paid salami pursuant to Settlement Case Nos. 48 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 152 for 0.0350 acres of land; 49 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 152 for 0.035 acres of land; 50 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 152 for 0.0350 acres of land; 51 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 152 for 0.0350 acres of land; 52 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 152 for 0.0350 acres of land; 53 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 151 for 0.0760 acres of land; 54 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 151 for 0.0767 acres of land; 55 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot No. 152 for 0.0650 acres of land; 56 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot Nos. 150 and 151 for 0.0766 acres of land; 57 of 2007-2008 in respect of Plot Nos. 140 and 150 for 0.150 acres of land. But after receiving the salami, in spite of repeated representations made by the petitioners, the Government has yet not executed and registered any deed of the lease in favour of the petitioners. Therefore, the petitioners having no other equally efficacious remedy filed the instant writ petition and obtained the Rule as stated above. 

 5. Mr Nawroz MR Chowdhury, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondent No. 1, Secretary, Ministry of Land submits that vide Memo No. ভূঃম/শা-৮/খাজব/৭৯০/২০০৫ (অংশ)/৩৩৬ dated 12-7-2009 and Memo No. ভূঃম/শা-৮/খাজব/৭৯০/২০০৫/১২০ dated 10-2-2010, the Ministry of land directed the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali to send a fresh proposal in respect of the approved and the unapproved settlement cases after holding a local inquiry and fixing the price of the land in question at the rate of present market value in accordance with the provisions of non-agricultural khas land management and settlement policy, 1995 which is under process. 

 6. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates from both the parties and perused the materials on record whereupon it transpires that the Government took a decision to settle unutilized 188.5 acres of khas land and accordingly a tender notice was published on 16-6-1999 fixing the price of the proposed land to be settled to the local inhabitants. A committee was formed headed by the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali for ascertaining and scrutinizing the heirs of the original owners of the acquired land and possessors of the acquired land. Accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali after holding an inquiry prepared a list to that effect and sent a recommendation to the Ministry of Land. The Ministry of Land directed the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali to lease out the proposed land as per Government circular dated 15-4-2007 and 15-6-2007. The Ministry of Land approved the name of 62 (sixty-two) persons including the name of the petitioners for leasing out the said 188.77 acres of land vide letters dated 22-7-2008 and 12-8-2008. At the instance of the petitioners, 10 (ten) settlement cases were opened in the office of respondent No. 5 as per directions and recommendations of the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali. Accordingly, the respondent No. 5 asked the petitioners to deposit the respective salami through DCR and they deposited the same to the Public Exchequer. Thereafter, respondent No. 5 directed all the petitioners to appear before him for executing Kabuliyat and accordingly all the petitioners went there but unfortunately the deeds were not been registered and executed as the respondent No. 2, Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali did not take appropriate steps to do the same. It appears that on 22-7-2008 and 12-8-2008 the Ministry of Land prepared a list and took a decision to settle the proposed land to the petitioners and other persons fixing the price of the land and the petitioners deposited the requisite money through DCR to the public fund. The subsequent decision of the Government for fixing the price of the land in question at the rate of present market value is not only unjust, unfair and unethical but also beyond the canon and rules of natural justice, since pursuant to the conclusive decision of the Government, the petitioners paid the salami in 2008 for getting the permanent lease of the land against their respective settlement cases. The Executive should not sit idle but do their public duties in accordance with the law. The citizens should not be placed at the capricious will of the Executive. There is no dispute about the settlement cases and the payment of salamis.
